data.why: No example data is bundled with the repo; wrote a small FASTA of 8 hand-made primers (normal, high-GC, low-Tm, one with an N ambiguity base, one very short, one longer) so the Bulk Analysis tab's batch QC scatter plot and table have realistic, varied input to exercise.

goals: Paste a single candidate primer sequence and read off its Tm, GC%, AT%, and molecular weight to decide if it is usable for PCR
Get the 5'-3' reverse complement of a primer to order the correct synthesis sequence
Upload a batch FASTA/txt file of candidate primers and screen dozens at once instead of calculating by hand
Use the GC% vs Tm scatter plot to spot outlier primers (e.g. extreme GC% or Tm) that are unlikely to work well in PCR
Check nucleotide composition visually to validate a primer isn't skewed or low-complexity
Export the full batch QC report as a CSV for record-keeping or ordering

review.summary: The tree captures the tool's purpose well: quick checks on one primer and batch QC before ordering, faithfully labelled, with a sensible single/batch structure. Twelve cited screens all match and every task and feature was replayed. It needs small fixes before filing: correct the 'complementary' wording, rework the weak 'look over the tool' phase, move the Fullscreen action to t10, and add coverage of silently dropped batch records and the actual accept/reject check (cutoffs, primer-pair Tm).
